messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Tagged Versions Naming Convention
parts:
If I checkout a tagged version of Stan I get library folders named
after each commit. For example, if I go to cmdstan and

git checkout v2.9.0
git submodule update —init —recursive

then I get the Stan library folder

stan_2.9.0.

The makefile points to the tagged library so everything should
work fine, but it’s confusing to have two Stan libraries around,
the tagged version and the regular “stan” folder that is carried
over from develop, no?

Moreover, when moving back to develop the tagged submodules
won’t be deleted because of their recursive nature (stan_2.9.0
can’t be deleted because it contained a tagged math library).
This has caused me no end of confusion this afternoon when
trying to do a regression test.

I don’t remember this behavior occurring previously — what is
the motivation?

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Tagged Versions Naming Convention
parts:
On Sun, Apr 17, 2016 at 1:14 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
If I checkout a tagged version of Stan I get library folders named
after each commit.  For example, if I go to cmdstan and

git checkout v2.9.0
git submodule update —init —recursive

then I get the Stan library folder

stan_2.9.0.

The makefile points to the tagged library so everything should
work fine, but it’s confusing to have two Stan libraries around,
the tagged version and the regular “stan” folder that is carried
over from develop, no?

The tagged version, v2.9.0, only points to stan_2.9.0 and not to stan. The "stan" folder you have left over when you check out that particular tag is due to git's conservative nature. In a perfect world, git would remove the "stan" folder and only leave "stan_2.9.0".

Moreover, when moving back to develop the tagged submodules
won’t be deleted because of their recursive nature (stan_2.9.0
can’t be deleted because it contained a tagged math library).
This has caused me no end of confusion this afternoon when
trying to do a regression test.
The same goes the other way.

I don’t remember this behavior occurring previously — what is
the motivation?

There were a few reasons for doing this -- I'm not sure any of them are really good reasons for continuing to do it:
- debugging users' configuration. Our initial concern was users substituting submodule branches and the developers chasing down bugs on stale branches. We haven't had many discussions on the stan-users list with users doing this, so it's not really a good reason.
- quick inspection and knowing what version we're looking at.
....

I thought there were more reasons, but I can't think of any right now. We thought more users would swap out branches and we'd spend time trying to find out what's going on when it's not really a Stan problem but with configuration. It just lives like that for a couple commits at each tag, but we don't have to do it that way. It would make tracking through the commits a little better. We already do some special things now when we tag which includes building the manual and checking that in so it's part of the distribution. I'm not sure how many people actually like having the user manual distributed in the tarball, but we could remove that too.


Daniel
